title: A natural abelian higher-direct-image sheafification comparison
statement: Fix a scheme $S$ [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions] and $p\in\mathbb N$. For every $h:Y\to S$ and abelian etale sheaf $F$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaves], put $P_{h,F}(U)=\operatorname{Hom}((h^{-1}\mathbb Z[U])[0],F[0][p])$, using [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image], [def-weil-pbc-sheafification] and [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories]. There is a family $e_{h,F}:P_{h,F}^{\#}\simeq R^p h_*F$ [def-weil-pbc-direct-image] with the following compatibility. For $a:Y'\to Y$, $h':Y'\to S$, $a\mathbin{\gg}h=h'$, and $\varphi:a^{-1}F\to F'$, define $b_a:P_{h,F}(U)\to P_{h',F'}(U)$ by the source pullback-composition comparison, inverse single-functor comparison, derived pullback of the class, pullback-shift comparison, and shifted single-functor comparison followed by $\varphi[0]$. The canonical map $M=\operatorname{abelianHigherDirectImageMap}(a,h,h',p,F,F',\varphi)$ [def-sbc-abelian-higher-direct-image-map] satisfies $M(U)((\eta\mathbin{\gg}e_{h,F})(z))=(\eta\mathbin{\gg}e_{h',F'})(b_a(z))$ for every etale $U\to S$ and $z\in P_{h,F}(U)$. The maps $b_a$ are explicitly constructed. No affine, qcqs or limit hypothesis is imposed.

proof.text: Construct the comparison by derived adjunction, homology, shift comparison and evaluation at the identity generator of the free abelian representable. The locally bijective cycle/boundary argument of the abelian higher-image presheaf theorem proves its sheafification invertible. Use the construction, not a choice from the abstract Nonempty conclusion. This construction is uniform in h and F.

Expand the adjunct of the raw class using the unit. Unit naturality moves the class across pullback, and the triangle identity cancels the intervening counit. Pullback composition and single-functor compatibility leave exactly the factors of the canonical higher-image transition; shift compatibility moves the coefficient map through the class. Apply degree-p homology and identity-generator evaluation to obtain the displayed compatibility.
